learningObjective: Understand ONNX as an interchange format distinct from runtimes; interchange ≠ peak performance.

canonicalClaims.claim: ONNX standardizes serialization, opset semantics, and shape/dtype info to enable model interchange; execution performance is entirely determined by the consuming runtime (ONNX Runtime, TensorRT, OpenVINO, IREE, etc.), which makes independent implementation choices.
nonImplications: Does not imply portability yields peak performance on any target.
Does not imply runtimes cannot share optimization tooling.

misconceptions.claim: Exporting to ONNX guarantees peak performance on any hardware.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Performance depends on the runtime, not the format.

misconceptions.claim: An `.onnx` file bundles a specific execution engine.
misconceptions.whyWrong: It is a data file; the runtime is a separate component.

misconceptions.claim: All ONNX-consuming runtimes produce identical numerical outputs.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Runtimes may produce slightly different results within spec tolerance (e.g., due to reduction order, mixed precision).

misconceptions.claim: ONNX Runtime and TensorRT are the same thing.
misconceptions.whyWrong: ONNX Runtime is Microsoft's runtime; TensorRT is NVIDIA's — both consume ONNX but are distinct products.

implementationFacts: ONNX Runtime, TensorRT, OpenVINO, IREE, TVM all consume ONNX with different pipelines.
Interchange format = portable representation; runtime = executor with its own optimizations.
performanceScenarios: Same ONNX file, different runtimes: latency can differ by orders of magnitude depending on hardware match, kernel availability, and fusion policy.
